parsed.explanation: Combined regime: state public-accommodation law, bias-crime response, and care-protection for travellers reduce ordinary in-state exposure. But federal border screening remains traveler-facing and cannot be cancelled: document mismatch, doubt, or suspected misrepresentation can trigger refusal, fraud findings, stranding, and possible immigration detention with documented abuse. Adult travellers face high entry/custody severity; adult-with-minor cases gain state school/healthcare protections but face unresolved federal hostility and local outting uncertainty. No execution documented.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal visa screening refuses applicants whose documents/records mismatch sex, requests more evidence, and can pursue permanent lifetime fraud ineligibility; trans/nonbinary travellers report blocked/confiscated passports and stranding abroad.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration; litigation, legal-aid FAQ and foreign advisories provide some relief, but no documented state immunity.
entry_documents.interaction: Visitor home-passport mismatch can trigger refusal, removal or fraud finding; state marker rules are resident-facing.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse; national corrections adopted conversion-therapy measures, including hair-cutting and HRT removal; trans prisoner counts not reported.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented visitor custody remedy; some federal orders enjoined; national hate-crime statute exists but does not reach visa screening.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry discrepancy can move into detention/fraud, where birth-sex placement or abusive custody becomes credible.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities; several states ban facilities and 4 criminalise in circumstances; arrest example elsewhere shows facility conflict can become trespass.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State public-accommodation law bars denial goods/services/lodging in hotels, restaurants, stores, transportation; state has no documented facility ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State protects private/state lodging/service but not federal facilities, border checkpoints or immigration detention.

care_services.exposure: National hostility includes funding freezes, proposed insurance bars for minors, youth-service shutdowns and subpoenas for patient records; care access can be disrupted outside protective state.
care_services.protection: State executive order directs agencies to protect gender-affirming healthcare within borders, including travellers from other jurisdictions; hospitals must protect SOGI data.
care_services.interaction: Care likely available in-state; federal insurance/facilities and emergency placement remain uncertain.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal orders and counterterrorism language use 'radical gender ideology' as hostile threat framing; local school-board outting policies are contested but unresolved.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State bars public-accommodation discrimination, enhances bias crimes, forbids gay-panic defence, police record SOGI and have sensitivity training.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State enforcement may deter street/service harm; federal agencies retain hostile posture and immigration screening.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal anti-minor orders threaten criminal support for social transition, funding cuts and record subpoenas; border mismatch applies to minors.
minors_guardians.protection: State school guidance supports names, pronouns, facilities and athletics; care protection for travelling minors; conversion therapy banned (climate).
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardians with trans minors may find school/healthcare safer in-state, but unresolved parental-outting policies and federal rules remain.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No documented pattern targeting trans visitors in-state; 2026 dataset places state among safest per-capita trans-woman killings.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State bias-crime enhancements, police SOGI reporting and sensitivity training; national hate-crime recourse exists.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local policing may respond protectively; travel through hostile federal facilities or other states raises risk.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Federal rules shift in litigation; enforcement of state anti-discrimination/bias-crime is not evidenced; school outting outcome unresolved; visitor detention remedy uncertain.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts blocked/enjoined some orders; civil-rights union sued; state civil-rights body investigates lodging/service complaints; legal-aid FAQ.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: State remedies may work for service denial/care, but likely cannot reverse border refusal, fraud findings or immigration custody.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar to 0.35-A for entry refusal without execution, but worse for fraud/stranding and possible immigration custody abuse; ordinary lodging/care is better because state public-accommodation and healthcare protections cover visitors.

Similar to 0.35-B at borders: document discrepancy triggers scrutiny or refusal. It exceeds 0.35-B in custody severity, but state service and bias-crime protections reduce everyday hotel/street humiliation.

Somewhat safer than 0.25-C for ordinary in-state visitors because the state lacks a facility ban and has care/service protections, but federal detention/corrections abuse and border screening remain comparably or more severe.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is bifurcated: once inside the protective state, lodging, public accommodations, bias-crime response and care access are shielded for adult and travelling-minor visitors. Federal entry screening nevertheless dominates the journey: passport/visa mismatch or officer doubt can trigger refusal, permanent fraud ineligibility, stranding, and possible immigration or corrections custody with documented severe abuse and care denial. State law does not create operative preemption over border, federal facilities, investigation, detention, or custody placement. Adult alone and adult-with-minor both remain elevated-to-high risk, with minors facing additional uncertainty from federal hostility, local parental-notification litigation, and unresolved care/school enforcement, while no execution is credibly documented.
